facts: $\sin\theta$ and $\sin\alpha$ can differ in the same triangle because the opposite and adjacent sides depend on the chosen angle, so a ratio must name its angle.
Two known sides tell you the ratio: opposite and hypotenuse $\rightarrow$ sine; adjacent and hypotenuse $\rightarrow$ cosine; opposite and adjacent $\rightarrow$ tangent.
steps: Label the sides relative to the marked angle
Write the ratio as a fraction of the two side lengths

workedExamples.solution_text:
The hypotenuse is $AC=35$.
(a) From $\angle BAC$, the adjacent side is $AB=28$.
$\cos(\angle BAC)=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{28}{35}=\frac45$.
(b) From $\angle ACB$, the opposite side is $AB=28$ and the adjacent side is $BC=21$.
$\tan(\angle ACB)=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=\frac{28}{21}=\frac43$.
Changing the reference angle swaps the opposite and adjacent sides; the hypotenuse stays the same.

workedExamples.question_text:
For each right-angled triangle described below, name the two given sides relative to $\theta$, choose the ratio that relates them, and write the equation. Do not calculate an unknown side.
(a) The side opposite $\theta$ is $9$ and the hypotenuse is $14$.
(b) The side next to $\theta$, excluding the hypotenuse, is $8$ and the hypotenuse is $11$.
(c) The side opposite $\theta$ is $q$ and the adjacent side is $7$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Opposite and hypotenuse use sine.
$\sin\theta=\frac{O}{H}=\frac{9}{14}$.
(b) Adjacent and hypotenuse use cosine.
$\cos\theta=\frac{A}{H}=\frac{8}{11}$.
(c) Opposite and adjacent use tangent.
$\tan\theta=\frac{O}{A}=\frac{q}{7}$.
Only tangent uses both shorter sides, so it can be written without knowing the hypotenuse.

foundation.question_text: Write the definition of $\cos\theta$ in terms of the sides of a right-angled triangle.

foundation.solution_text:
The sides are named from $\alpha$, so the adjacent side is the vertical one.
$\cos\alpha$
$=\dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
$=\dfrac{9}{15}$
$=\dfrac{3}{5}$

The labelled sides are the opposite ($4$) and the hypotenuse ($7$).
Opposite with hypotenuse is the sine ratio.
$\sin\theta$
$=\dfrac{4}{7}$

development.solution_text:
The labelled sides are the adjacent ($9$) and the hypotenuse ($12$).
Adjacent with hypotenuse is the cosine ratio.
$\cos\theta$
$=\dfrac{9}{12}$
$=\dfrac{3}{4}$

The labelled sides are the opposite ($x$) and the adjacent ($6$).
Opposite with adjacent is the tangent ratio.
$\tan\theta$
$=\dfrac{x}{6}$

The sides are named from $\alpha$, so the opposite side is the horizontal one.
$\sin\alpha$
$=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
$=\dfrac{21}{29}$

mastery.solution_text:
The labelled sides are the opposite ($11$) and the adjacent ($12$); the hypotenuse is not given.
Sine and cosine both need the hypotenuse, so only the tangent ratio can be written.
$\tan\theta$
$=\dfrac{11}{12}$

mastery.question_text:
In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC=90^{\circ}$, $AB=20$, $BC=21$ and $AC=29$.
Write $\cos(\angle ACB)$ and $\tan(\angle BAC)$ as fractions.
mastery.solution_text:
The hypotenuse is $AC=29$, opposite the right angle at $B$.
From $\angle ACB$ the adjacent side is $BC=21$.
$\cos(\angle ACB)=\dfrac{21}{29}$
From $\angle BAC$ the opposite side is $BC=21$ and the adjacent side is $AB=20$.
$\tan(\angle BAC)=\dfrac{21}{20}$
